reason: This device mainly provides an extra pull-down/loading path on the internal node net018; removing it usually keeps the core left/right amplification paths intact (M6/M7 driving the PMOS loads to VOUT1/VOUT2). Caveat: net018 may float more, so biasing of the VOUT2-side PMOS load can shift and dynamic behavior can change.

This is a diode-connected PMOS that behaves like a bias/helper for net018; if net018 can be biased by other circuitry or you accept net018 being less regulated, it can be removed while preserving basic gain through the remaining load devices. Caveat: VOUT2 DC operating point and gain may drift; matching/symmetry degrades.

This is a VOUT2 pull-down controlled by net015; if the output load or testbench provides a discharge/return path (or you only care about VOUT1), deleting it often still leaves a functioning amplification path. Caveat: VOUT2 can become less defined (swing/CM level), and slew/settling can worsen.
impact_estimate: Low if VOUT2 is unused or externally loaded; moderate otherwise
